title: Jobs: Is the impact of AI on jobs heating up?
description: Send us Fan Mail This week on "Preparing for AI," we tackle the sobering reality of job displacement due to AI advancements and the ethical dilemmas that come with new technologies. We kick off with a deep dive into Microsoft's Copilot Plus PCs, machines equipped with neural processing units to handle AI workloads locally. Imagine your computer not only working smarter but maintaining functionality even offline. Yet, there's a catch—constant snapshots of your activities raise significant privacy concerns. We weigh the benefits against the potential risks, shedding light on the future of user privacy in an AI-driven world. The conversation then shifts to the real-world consequences of AI on employment. The stories are stark: a graphic designer and a copywriter find themselves out of work, replaced by AI tools like MidJourney and DALL-E. These aren't isolated incidents. Major corporations like British Telecom and IBM are aggressively incorporating AI into their operations, leading to massive workforce reductions. British Telecom plans to cut 40% of its jobs by 2030, while IBM has paused hiring for non-customer-facing roles. We scrutinize these unsettling trends, unpacking what they mean for the future of work and the human cost of technological progress. By interviewing somebody recently affected by job cuts we examine the seismic shifts in digital content creation brought on by AI. Traditional journalists face mounting tension as AI-generated content becomes more prevalent, reshaping everything from SEO strategies to consumer preferences. Younger audiences are increasingly comfortable with AI-generated voiceovers on platforms like TikTok, signaling a generational shift in content consumption. We also delve into the philosophical and legislative challenges posed by AI, discussing Universal Basic Income and Universal High Income as potential solutions to job displacement. And to wrap it all up, we recommend Lazy Owl's YouTube video for a glimpse into a balanced society where AI and humans could coexist productively. Join us for a comprehensive look into the social impacts of AI and step ahead of the curve in preparing for the future. Apologies in advance for the poor audio quality on some of this week's episode. Links from this episode: Anthropic Golden Gate Bridge: https://www.anthropic.com/news/golden-gate-claude Neural Networks: https://www.3blue1brown.com/topics/neural-networks Lazy Owl Video: https://youtu.be/iNKFOCki42I?si=kjxP1sl_zCCDDV1a
summary: The hosts argue the pace of AI job losses has stepped up: viral first-person accounts from a graphic designer (nade straight, ~750k views) and a copywriter (Ashen Guardian), plus hard corporate announcements — BT cutting ~40% of roles by 2028-2030 with 10,000 direct AI replacements, and IBM pausing non-customer-facing hiring (~7,800 roles). An anonymous publishing veteran describes senior editorial jobs replaced by junior 'social and AI' hires, Google AI answers gutting referral traffic, and generative content convergence, before Hinton's UBI plea and Musk's 'universal high income' close the episode.
keyTalkingPoints: Microsoft Copilot Plus PCs add an NPU plus 'Recall' snapshots of everything — useful but a privacy own goal; on-device LLMs are the positive
Anthropic's Golden Gate Claude: amplifying one feature gave the model an identity crisis — the first real look inside a frontier model
BT: 130k staff to 75-80k by 2028-30 (40%), including 10,000 roles as direct AI replacements; IBM: hiring freeze on ~7,800 back-office roles
Anonymous guest: it is senior jobs going, replaced by juniors with 'social and AI experience'; Google AI overviews slash referral traffic
If trained writers cannot earn, models run out of lived-experience data; all content converges on generic AI output
Hinton told Sunak to introduce UBI now; Musk pitched 'universal high income'; Lazy Owl video offers a Culture-like third way

jimmy: We are at a paradigm shift: companies now openly say AI replaces jobs, and that normalization will spread
Agentic models like Devin 'don't really work' yet — they loop and burn money; junior developers are most exposed
If everyone drafts with ChatGPT, all content converges into the same generic output
Global poverty should be fixed before anyone gets a universal high income
matt: Stealth cuts lull people into false security — named cuts at least let people act; uncertainty is the worst part
AI chips on laptops enabling offline models are potentially really positive; security concerns will limit early adoption
Most companies will chase cost savings, so governments must legislate — and it will be reactive and too late for many
Recommends funeral directing as AI-proof work; finds Lazy Owl's third scenario a genuinely hopeful vision
